spatial_disposition.evidence: Chihuahua State Government (https://chihuahua.gob.mx/conoce-chihuahua/personajes-ilustres) explicitly treats Chihuahua as a Mexican state and Villa as its 1913–1914 governor, and INEHRM (https://www.inehrm.gob.mx/es/inehrm/villa) dates entry and administration to 8 Dec 1913. The request does not establish a reviewed historical PolityPlaceFunction, canonical Place UUID, exact 1913–14 territorial extent, or display binding; geographic representation remains reviewed_hold. This subnational Mexican constituent state must not be presented as an independent Villa-created sovereign country.

activity.notes: Francisco 'Pancho' Villa (born José Doroteo Arango Arámbula; 1878–1923) assumed military gubernatorial powers over the Mexican federal constituent State of Chihuahua on 8 December 1913 after occupation by the División del Norte. His administration set food price controls, confiscated holdings of the anti-revolutionary oligarchy and founded the Chihuahua state bank. INEHRM dates Carranza's appointment of Manuel Chao to 7 January 1914, while Chihuahua state government's commemorative history describes Villa's handover as 8 January 1914. This approximate 7 January end is an administrative boundary convention, not an independently proven instantaneous handover; state power and later de facto control are distinct from the formal gubernatorial office. The new State of Chihuahua polity is a Mexican constituent state, not an independent sovereign polity or a new state founded by Villa.

sources.title: INEHRM — Francisco Villa: Cronología de la Revolución
sources.citation_text: The Mexican National Institute for Historical Studies of the Revolutions dates Villa's assumption of Chihuahua state government to 8 December 1913 and Carranza's appointment of Manuel Chao as governor to 7 January 1914. It documents his four weeks of governor policy and the 1913 Chihuahua bank.

sources.title: Gobierno del Estado de Chihuahua — Personajes ilustres: Francisco Villa
sources.citation_text: Chihuahua State Government records Villa's approximately one-month governorship after 1913 and describes transfer of the governorship to General Manuel Chao on 8 January 1914. It identifies land and price policies and the state bank.
